# fluss-go v0.2.0-beta.4

This maintenance beta improves cancellation, delivery correctness, input
ownership, and writer failure reporting for Apache Fluss 1.0. It adds no
exported API and does not change the Fluss wire formats or Go baseline.

## Upgrade

- Apache Fluss 0.9.1 users must remain on fluss-go `v0.1.0-beta.11`.
- Apache Fluss `1.0.0` and Go `1.26.11` or later supported Go 1.26 patches
  remain required. This is still an experimental beta, not a stable v1 API.
- Upgrade the root and any HDFS, OSS, OpenTelemetry, or S3 adapters together
  to `v0.2.0-beta.4`.
- Review the [beta.3 upgrade guidance](https://github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/blob/v0.2.0-beta.4/docs/migration-v0.2.md#upgrading-from-v020-beta3)
  before rollout. In particular, `Flush` and `Close` now return retained
  background batch errors; repeated barriers do not clear them. A canceled
  `Close` that has not submitted shutdown must be retried with a live context.
- A typed-nil `*big.Rat` is rejected with `ErrInvalidRow`, not converted to
  SQL NULL. Use untyped `nil` for NULL and a non-nil decimal pointer for zero.

```sh
go get github.com/pletorco/fluss-go@v0.2.0-beta.4
go get github.com/pletorco/fluss-go/adapters/s3@v0.2.0-beta.4
go mod tidy
```

## Highlights

- Preserve undelivered log records after cancellation or `Wakeup`, and retain
  KV pages across decoding or historical-schema lookup failures. Retrying a
  recoverable poll no longer skips the received data.
- Retain original background batch errors across writer `Flush` and `Close`,
  including already completed failures and poisoned-bucket error chains.
- Make transport frame admission and writer command admission cancelable,
  without interrupting accepted work or leaking a rejected input's slot.
- Snapshot append row/key bytes before `Append` returns, including mutable
  nested values and decimals. Indexed batch sizing uses actual indexed bytes.
  Arrow batch retention requirements are unchanged.
- Isolate returned and cached schema metadata. Append writers prepare an
  owned schema once, reducing repeated validation allocations while still
  checking every input value. Performance gains are workload-specific.
- Reject typed-nil decimals before encoding or queuing, including nested
  values and decimal keys, rather than panicking.
- Pin Trivy to `v0.76.2` and run CVE checks daily. Failed scans and newer-stable
  Trivy releases fail the scheduled workflow and update a deduplicated alert
  issue; this does not add a runtime dependency to client applications.
- Replace the withdrawn MinIO test image with official RustFS `1.0.6`, pinned
  by digest. The existing S3 adapter assertions are retained. This changes
  test infrastructure only, not production object storage or Go dependencies.

## Deliberate boundaries

Historical physical-partition routing for lake workflows remains unsupported.
Native Iceberg, Lance, and Paimon planning remains application-owned. This
release is a pure-Go client and does not link or wrap the Fluss Rust core.

## Verification and publication

The completed release-preparation branch must pass `task ci`, the local
`task sonar` Quality Gate, `task test:integration`, and `task test:storage`.
Unit, golden, fuzz-smoke, race, generation, API, documentation, security, and
license checks remain required. Live compatibility targets Apache Fluss
`1.0.0` commit `5c07f88e50a8ff41b0ebc214a0458e5dba60be37`, image digest
`sha256:ff461b45438033da4fd1c2556d3f978f3603bb3632fe075c2bd57388339a58cb`.

Do not publish tags before the release-preparation PR is approved and merged.
Publish the root first, verify it through the public Go module proxy, then
publish all four path-prefixed adapter tags on that same reviewed commit.
